items.prompt: Merge overlapping intervals first step is usually?
choices: Hash endpoints into a set and stop
DFS the intervals as a graph always
items.whyRight: Sorted starts let one sweep merge overlaps.
whyWrong: Length alone does not order overlaps.
Graphs are optional for some variants, not the merge baseline.

items.prompt: After sorting by start, merge when?
items.whyRight: Overlap or touch (per problem statement) extends the active interval.
whyWrong: Disjoint next starts close the previous interval.

items.prompt: Meeting rooms / min concurrency often uses?
choices: Sweep line on sorted start/end events
items.whyRight: +1 on start, −1 on end; track peak active count.

items.prompt: Insert interval into a sorted disjoint list?
choices: Walk, merge while overlapping the newcomer, splice the result
Resort the entire list after naive append always as the only way
items.whyRight: Linear scan around the overlap region is enough.
whyWrong: Full resort works but hides the merge structure.

items.prompt: Non-overlapping removal classic greedy sorts by?
choices: End time and keeps earliest-finishing compatible intervals
Start time only without further rule
items.whyRight: Same exchange argument as interval scheduling.

items.prompt: Why sort+sweep is O(n log n)?
choices: Sorting dominates; the sweep is linear
items.whyRight: After O(n log n) sort, one pass merges or counts.
